newsitem.title: UK: Brown cuts small company tax rate, boosts allowance.
newsitem.headline: Brown cuts small company tax rate, boosts allowance.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced he was cutting the tax rate for small companies to 21 percent from 23 percent from April 1997.
He is also doubling for one year the level of first year capital allowance on plant and machinery for small and medium-sized firms for both companies and unincorporated businesses.

"The route to success is not for the government to try to pluck winners but to create an environment in which more firms have more chances by their own efforts to succeed," he told parliament in his budget speech. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 5109
